sources.title: TodoMVC behavior reference: precise functional contract

model.vision: A dependable todo list that a small team can start using tomorrow.
model.mission: Keep every team member's todos in one dependable, team-owned record that outlives any session, and let people and the team's assistants work that same record through whichever channel they already use. Hold the experience to the familiar, well-known todo-list behavior so it needs no learning and every action takes a single step.

items.definition: A person on the team who keeps their own todos in the list and acts on them.
An automated helper the team already uses that acts on a team member's todo list on their behalf, with the same abilities a person has.
A single thing a team member intends to do, described by its title and either active or completed.
The free-text wording that says what a todo is; it is never blank.
The state of a todo that has not been done yet.
The state of a todo the team member has marked as done.
The full, ordered set of a team member's todos, in the order they were added.
Put a new active todo with a given title at the end of the todo list.
Change the wording of an existing todo without removing and re-adding it; retitling to blank removes the todo instead.
Take one todo off the todo list for good, whatever its state, leaving every other todo as it was.
Mark one todo as done, leaving every other todo as it was.
Mark one completed todo as not done again, leaving every other todo as it was.
In one step, mark every todo completed — or, when every todo is already completed, mark every todo active again.
In one step, take every completed todo off the todo list, leaving active todos untouched.
Which todos the team member chooses to see: All, Active, or Completed; choosing a view never changes any todo.
The number of active todos on the whole todo list, always current and independent of the chosen view.
A team member coming back to the todo list later and finding it exactly as they left it.
Business activity: deciding whether submitted wording is a usable title — wording that is empty or only spaces is not a title.
Business activity: deciding whether Toggle All completes everything or reopens everything, based on whether every todo is already completed.
Business activity: picking out the todos that belong in the chosen view from the whole todo list.
Business activity: counting the active todos across the whole todo list to produce items left.
Resource access: keep a newly added todo in the team's durable record of the todo list.
Resource access: replace the recorded title of one todo.
Resource access: take one todo out of the recorded todo list.
Resource access: set the recorded state of one todo to active or completed.
Resource access: set the recorded state of every todo on the list to the same state in one step.
Resource access: take every completed todo out of the recorded todo list in one step.
Resource access: bring back the recorded todo list, with each todo's title and state, in the order the todos were added.
The team-owned, durable keeping place for each team member's todo list; it outlives any visit, closed window, or restart.

items.name: Assistant-protocol volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the protocol through which the team's assistants and other agent tooling reach the todo list (today an ordinary web API and an MCP surface). WHY: agent-tooling protocols are young and churn fast — MCP itself and its revisions arrived within the last couple of years, and the team already says it adopts whatever its 'other agent tooling' speaks. LIKELIHOOD: high — at least one new or revised assistant protocol per year inside the system's lifespan. EFFECT: if each protocol carried its own copy of add/retitle/remove/complete/toggle-all/clear-completed/view/items-left logic, every protocol change would ripple into every behavior and the people and assistants would drift onto inconsistent rules; encapsulated, a new protocol is a new entry point onto the same behaviors.

items.name: Human-presentation volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: the screens and the host they are rendered in for team members (today an ordinary web app plus an embedded MCP Apps surface). WHY: the founder wants the UI embedded 'the same way our other MCP-hosted UIs are', so presentation follows whatever hosts the team adopts; embedding hosts and their UI rules change independently of the todo behaviors and at a different rate from assistant protocols. LIKELIHOOD: medium-high — a new host or major host change every year or two. EFFECT: unencapsulated, gesture details (Enter to commit, Escape to cancel, visible current view) and host rules would leak into the todo rules, so every new host forces re-implementing and re-verifying all nine behaviors.

items.name: Change-propagation volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: how and when an actor working the list through one channel learns of changes another actor made through a different channel (refresh on return, polling, pushed live updates). WHY: the mission puts people and assistants on the same record at once, and items-left must be current after every change; as the team leans more on assistants, more changes happen out from under an open screen. LIKELIHOOD: medium — expectations move from 'correct on return visit' to 'live' as assistant use grows over 1-3 years. EFFECT: baked into each channel, every move toward live updates touches every behavior that changes active/completed state and the items-left tally.

items.name: Actor-identity volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: how a team member is recognized and how a team assistant is authorized to act on that member's list on their behalf. WHY: each member keeps their own list and assistants act with the same abilities as a person, but teams differ in how they identify people (company sign-in, simple accounts) and how they delegate to agents (tokens, delegated grants). LIKELIHOOD: high across teams today and rising as agent-delegation conventions settle. EFFECT: unencapsulated, the identity scheme threads through every channel and every access to the record, so changing it means touching every behavior.

items.name: Record-storage volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: where and in what kind of keeping place the team-owned durable record of each list lives. WHY: the record must outlive any visit, closed window, or service restart and be team-owned, but teams keep their data in different places (a single-file store for a trial tomorrow, a managed database later, a self-hosted store for teams that must own their data). LIKELIHOOD: high — the very first move from 'try it tomorrow' to 'use it for real' changes it. EFFECT: unencapsulated, every record/reword/strike/mark/purge/recall access carries storage specifics, so a storage change ripples through all state-changing behaviors and the return-visit guarantee.

items.name: Hosting-environment volatility
items.rationale: WHAT: where and how the service runs — a laptop or single box for the trial, then the team's standard infrastructure 'the way we build everything else here'. WHY: the founder's delivery constraint and 'start using tomorrow' guarantee at least one hosting move early, and house infrastructure itself changes every few years. LIKELIHOOD: near-certain within the first year. EFFECT: if hosting assumptions (process lifetime, configuration, network exposure) leak into the behaviors, each move risks the return-visit guarantee and forces changes across the service; this is expected to be encapsulated largely by operational concepts rather than a component.

rejected.name: Title-acceptance rule volatility
rejected.reason: Whether wording is a usable title (not empty or whitespace-only, perhaps a length cap later) is one predicate; any tweak is a conditional change in one place, not an architectural ripple.

rejected.name: Toggle-all decision rule volatility
rejected.reason: 'Complete all unless all are already completed, then reopen all' is the TodoMVC contract that every implementation follows identically; changing it would change what the product is.

rejected.name: Clear-completed semantics volatility
rejected.reason: Removing every completed todo and leaving active ones untouched is identical across every todo app; there is no plausible variant to encapsulate.

rejected.name: View set volatility (All/Active/Completed)
rejected.reason: The three views are selection predicates over completed state; another state-based view would be one more predicate, handled by data or a conditional.

rejected.name: Items-left counting volatility
rejected.reason: Counting active todos across the whole list is a fixed computation; only how fast it reaches other screens changes, which is folded into change-propagation volatility.

rejected.name: Todo ordering volatility
rejected.reason: Lists keep todos in the order they were added in every TodoMVC implementation; drag-to-reorder is explicitly out of scope.

rejected.name: Todo-attribute volatility (due dates, priorities, tags)
rejected.reason: The contract explicitly says due dates, priorities and tags must not be assumed required; encapsulating for them would design for a different product.

rejected.name: List-sharing / ownership volatility
rejected.reason: Multi-user sharing is explicitly out of scope; each member keeps their own list, and nothing in the brief suggests shared lists are coming.

rejected.name: Undo/redo history volatility
rejected.reason: Undo/redo is explicitly out of scope; the only 'undo' asked for is re-toggling, which the toggle behaviors already cover.

rejected.name: Offline-sync volatility
rejected.reason: Offline sync is explicitly out of scope, and the founder wants the record kept by the real service, not on the client.

rejected.name: Reminder/notification volatility
rejected.reason: Nothing in the brief or contract mentions reminders or notifications; adding a notification seam would be by reflex.

rejected.name: Reporting block
rejected.reason: Siren-song habit: no stakeholder asked for reports on todos; the only figure needed is items left, which is part of the core behavior.

rejected.name: Audit logging block
rejected.reason: Siren-song habit: no requirement for an activity history or audit trail of who changed which todo; ordinary diagnostics are a utility concern, not a business volatility.

rejected.name: UI language/localization volatility
rejected.reason: A small single team; any translation of labels is resource-string data handled inside presentation, not a structural change.

rejected.name: Edit gesture volatility (Enter/Escape/blur, double-click)
rejected.reason: How an edit is started, committed, or cancelled is a property of each screen and host; folded into human-presentation volatility.

rejected.name: MCP Apps embedding-host volatility
rejected.reason: The embedding host is one of the presentation hosts; the same underlying change as human-presentation volatility.

rejected.name: Web API versioning volatility
rejected.reason: Changes to the ordinary web API that assistants and tooling call are the same underlying change as assistant-protocol volatility.

rejected.name: Assistant capability-scope volatility
rejected.reason: Whether an assistant gets the full abilities of a person or a narrower set is a question of delegated authority; folded into actor-identity volatility.

rejected.name: Durability-guarantee volatility
rejected.reason: How strongly the record must survive restarts is set by where and how it is kept; folded into record-storage volatility.

rejected.name: Concurrent-edit conflict volatility
rejected.reason: A person and an assistant changing the same todo near-simultaneously is the same underlying concern as how changes reach other actors; folded into change-propagation volatility.

rejected.name: Load/scale volatility
rejected.reason: A small team trying the app has trivial load; designing for scale now would be for a hypothetical larger business.

decisions.essenceRationale: Every way a todo list ever changes — adding, rewording, removing, completing, reopening, completing or reopening everything, sweeping away the finished — is one business act: a recognized team member, or an assistant acting for them, changes the team-owned record of their list and everyone working that list learns the result. It is shared by every customer (person or assistant, any channel, any storage), it is nearly immutable (the TodoMVC contract has fixed these rules for a decade), and it is what makes this product dependable rather than a toy: the change lands in a record that outlives any session and is the same no matter which channel made it. The six customer verbs are permutations of the change; the abstraction is the durable, channel-independent change itself.

The channel shows the chosen view, marks it as current, and shows items left; no todo is changed

decisions.essenceRationale: Seeing one's list — in whichever view, with an always-true count of what is left, exactly as it was left on the last visit — is the other half of every todo product and the half every customer uses most. It is shared by all customers and all channels, it does not change over time (All/Active/Completed and items-left are fixed by the contract), and it carries the product's differentiating promise of a team-owned record that is never lost: a return visit, a filter switch and a glance at the counter are all the same act of recalling the durable list and presenting a selection and tally of it. It never changes any todo, which is why it is a distinct core from working the list.

verdicts.summary:
BLOCKING (1): Toggle-all rule has two homes. DynamicView "work-the-todo-list", step n16 draws one call, todo-keeping-manager → todo-list-access "MarkEveryTodo(member, completed) — completes all, or reopens all when all are completed". That label makes TodoListAccess the owner of the toggle-all decision. DynamicView "mark-everything-done-at-once-and-undo-it" puts the same decision in the Manager: n4 calls TallyItemsLeft(member), then n5/n6 call MarkEveryTodo(member, completed=false|true) as a plain write. These describe the same work at different granularities and give the RA contract two meanings (does MarkEveryTodo decide, or does it just write?). That is a cross-view symmetry defect and a business rule leaking into ResourceAccess, so construction can't honestly implement it. Fix: in work-the-todo-list n16, draw the same idiom the variation uses. The Manager calls TallyItemsLeft(member) → count to settle "are all already completed?", then MarkEveryTodo(member, completed=…) as an atomic write. Drop "completes all, or reopens all when all are completed" from the RA call label. Keep MarkEveryTodo on TodoListAccess as a pure atomic verb. Don't reshape the decomposition or the use case for this; it is a drawing-level correction.

NON-BLOCKING (record or answer on the redraft; these don't by themselves justify revise):
(a) Review idiom reads the store twice. In review-the-todo-list, switch-between-all-active-and-done-todos, find-the-list-as-it-was-left-on-returning and use-the-todo-list-embedded-in-an-mcp-hosted-screen, RecallList(member) hops to todo-store ("read the member's todos in added order"), and then SelectInView(member, view) hops to todo-store again ("read the member's todos matching the view"). Nothing visibly uses RecallList's result. Either say what the Manager does with the recalled list (e.g. the returned payload carries both the whole list and the view), or have SelectInView select over the recalled todos, so neither call is drawn just to cover a node.
(b) The Manager name TodoKeepingManager echoes the system/swimlane name rather than the change it contains (sequencing a change → re-tally → make it known). It's acceptable for a single-Manager system, but consider a name that answers "what change does this contain?".
(c) Change propagation: the publish(ListChanged) seam on message-bus is honest, and drawing it on every "make the change known" node is the right single edge. No subscriber side is modelled, so .operationalConcepts must explicitly resolve how Clients receive ListChanged (refresh/poll/push). Carry that as a stated deferral.
(d) Hosting-environment volatility as a typed facet of TodoListAccess is acceptable, given the committed rationale says it is "encapsulated largely by operational concepts". Keep the explicit operational-concepts deferral for process lifetime, configuration and exposure.
Accepted as justified: 1 Manager / 0 Engines (every rule candidate was rejected in .volatilities). Single-surface entry on the embedded use case, and machine-only entry on the agent-tooling use case, both follow from those use cases' definitions. The sweep and add guards draw no call. No ambient edges. Layering is closed throughout.

verdicts.summary:
BLOCKING — objectives are empty. The stored Mission model has 7 objective entries, but every one is {"number": 0, "statement": ""} (checked in getDraftSlot and directly in .aiarch/state/project.json). Your commit message lists O1–O7 (capture/edit/delete; toggle/toggle-all; clear completed; filters + active count; persistence; people + agents on the same list; adoption right away), but none of that text got saved. Without objectives the Mission has no WHY, and the vision and mission can't be traced to anything. Re-save the model so each objective is numbered 1–7 and has a non-empty statement.

While you re-save, write each objective as a business reason, not a feature. Ch. 5 says objectives are WHY the business wants the vision. Several of the commit-message items (O1–O4: capture/edit/delete, toggle, clear completed, filters/count) are required behaviors, not business objectives. Reword them as outcomes, e.g. "No team member ever loses a todo they recorded", "The team's assistants and its people act on one shared list, so nothing is tracked twice", "A new team member is productive on day one with no training". You may also merge them into fewer objectives. Keep everything in business/user language, with no component, service, layer or other decomposition words.

Vision and mission pass, so no changes needed there. The vision is one terse sentence of 13 words with no benefit-tail. The mission states a recognizable HOW: one dependable team-owned record that outlives any session, worked through whatever channel each person or assistant already uses, kept to familiar one-step todo behavior. It does not restate the vision, and it has no architecture terms.

actorIdentityAccess.title: ActorIdentityAccess — recognizes the team member behind a presented proof (directly, or through an assistant's delegation grant), or refuses it

ActorProof.description: A neutral, opaque credential the client channel received from the actor: either a member's own proof or an assistant's delegation grant. The caller passes it through untouched; it is never logged or echoed.

credential.description: The opaque credential text as presented by the actor.

Recognition.description: The outcome of recognition. Fail-closed: recognized is true only when the proof or grant was positively verified.

memberID.description: Opaque, stable identity of the recognized member (the delegating member when an assistant acts). Empty when refused.

onBehalf.description: True when a team assistant is acting under the member's delegation grant (for audit only; the assistant has the member's abilities).

recognized.description: True when the actor is recognized as a team member.

actorIdentityAccess.notes:
Designer: senior-developer (detailed design); reviewer: system-architect. Implementer: junior-developer.

Operation RecognizeActor(proof) -> Recognition, error.
- Pre: proof carries the opaque credential the actor presented. Post: Recognition says member (memberID, onBehalf) or refused (refusal reason). Side effects: none (read-only verification against team-identity-provider over HTTP).
- A refusal is a normal result, not an error: bad/expired/revoked/unverifiable proofs -> recognized=false, refusal=unrecognized; provider unreachable or timed out -> recognized=false, refusal=unavailable. The returned error is reserved for invariant/programming faults (e.g. misconfiguration) and is terminal. Fail closed: never return a default member.
- An assistant's delegation grant resolves to the delegating member only (onBehalf=true); never to any other member.
- Idempotent and safe to retry: same proof -> same outcome while the provider's verdict is unchanged. No caching of verification results in the first release (revocation freshness over latency).
- Retryability: refusal=unavailable is transient (caller may retry); unrecognized is terminal. Orchestration guidance (advisory): bounded wait ~2s per call to the provider.
- Security: never log or echo credential text; treat provider responses as untrusted input.
- Callers: todo-keeping-manager only, sync, first step of all 13 dynamic views. Publishes/subscribes nothing; no queued ops (ResourceAccess).

Factoring: one facet (actor recognition). The System assigns this component the single atomic business verb RecognizeActor and every dynamic view calls only that; TP-OP-REACHED forbids uncalled ops, so no further operations are added.

messageBus.title: MessageBus contract

Message.description: One change notice handed to the bus. The bus treats it as opaque routing data: it never interprets the topic or scope beyond matching them. The publisher (TodoKeepingManager) owns the meaning, e.g. topic "ListChanged" with scope = the member whose list changed. It carries no todo content.

scope.description: Opaque id of the owner the notice concerns (the member id for ListChanged). Non-empty. Delivery is confined to this scope so one member's notices never reach another member's actors.

topic.description: Name of the notice kind, e.g. ListChanged. Non-empty.

messageBus.notes:
STATUS: FROZEN, once architect review passes. DESIGNER: senior-developer. REVIEWER: system-architect.

FACET: one contract, MessageBus: fire-and-forget publication of change notices. Utility layer: message-agnostic plumbing with no business volatility of its own. It serves the Change-propagation volatility, which TodoKeepingManager owns: the Manager decides what counts as a change and when to announce it, and the bus only carries the notice. Sole caller: TodoKeepingManager, synchronously, as the last step of every state-changing use case (work-the-todo-list n19, add-a-todo n9, fix-a-todo-s-wording n9, remove-a-todo n6, mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done n6, mark-everything-done-at-once-and-undo-it n9, sweep-away-finished-todos n9, let-the-team-s-agent-tooling-drive-the-list n6). The bus calls no other component, reaches no Resource, and imports no Temporal.

OPERATIONS:
- Publish(message) error: hands one notice to the bus and returns at once. Pre: message.topic and message.scope are non-empty. Post: the notice has been accepted for delivery to whatever subscribers exist for that topic and scope. Publish never blocks on a subscriber, never waits for delivery, and never reports a subscriber's failure to the publisher. It is safe for concurrent use.

- ErrInvalidMessage (terminal): empty topic or empty scope.
- ErrBusUnavailable (transient): the bus is shut down, or its transport can't accept the notice right now.

No dynamic view calls it, so methodcheck TP-OP-REACHED would refuse it, and no consumer is modelled in the committed System (SRS Q1). When a use case adds a subscriber, the architect adds the edge and this contract gains Subscribe as a revision. A typed ListChanged payload was rejected in favour of an opaque topic and scope. Encapsulates change-propagation volatility: the fixed sequence recognize -> change -> tally -> make known, and how the other channels learn of a change. Downstream (all sync): actor-identity-access.RecognizeActor, todo-list-access (RecordTodo, RewordTodo, StrikeTodo, MarkTodo, MarkEveryTodo, PurgeCompleted, RecallList, SelectInView, TallyItemsLeft), message-bus.Publish. Calls no Engine (none exists), no other Manager; nothing queued. Publishes ListChanged via MessageBus; subscribes to nothing.

EXECUTION MODEL: plain synchronous in-process Manager; every public op is a request/response call, not a Temporal Workflow/Signal/Query/Update. Rationale: operational concepts are not committed, the SRS fixes every inbound and outbound edge as sync with nothing queued, the Manager is stateless between calls, and load/scale volatility was rejected — there is no long-running, durable or resumable workflow to host. Therefore it registers no Activities and imports no Temporal. If operational concepts later make the Manager Temporal-hosted, each op maps 1:1 to an Update (validated write with response) and ReviewList to a Query, with one Activity per downstream RA call (TodoListAccess guidance: StartToClose 5s, retry only ErrRecordUnavailable; ActorIdentityAccess ~2s, retry only refusal=unavailable) — that is a revision, not a contract-shape change.

COMMON PRELUDE (every op, step n3 of all 13 views): RecognizeActor(proof). recognized=false, refusal=unrecognized -> return ErrActorRefused; refusal=unavailable -> return ErrIdentityUnavailable. On refusal touch nothing: no read, no write, no tally, no publish, and the error reveals nothing about the list. The member used for every downstream call is ONLY Recognition.memberID — no op accepts a member id from the caller, so a caller can never name another member; an assistant (onBehalf=true) acts with exactly the delegating member's abilities and rules.

COMMON POSTLUDE (every state-changing op, after the change is committed): TallyItemsLeft(member) -> itemsLeft returned to the caller (reflects this request's change); then Publish({topic: "ListChanged", scope: memberID}). ListChanged carries member scope only — no todo content, no counts. Publish is fire-and-forget: a Publish error is logged (without credential or titles) and the request still SUCCEEDS, because the change is persisted and readers re-read on return. Publish never runs before the change is committed.

USABLE-TITLE RULE (plain Manager logic; title-acceptance was ruled variableNotVolatile): trim leading/trailing whitespace; the title is usable iff the trimmed text is non-empty. The trimmed text is what is stored. No length cap in this release.

OPERATIONS (error model: package sentinels checked with errors.Is, below):
- AddTodo(proof, title) -> AddOutcome. Views: add-a-todo, work-the-todo-list, let-the-team-s-agent-tooling-drive-the-list. Usable -> RecordTodo(member, trimmed) -> accepted=true, todo=the recorded todo. Unusable -> nothing recorded, accepted=false, todo zero value; per the committed activity graph (n6 merges into n7) the refused path still re-tallies and publishes (a no-change ListChanged is harmless: notices coalesce to 're-read'). A refused add is a normal outcome, not an error. Not idempotent (each accepted call appends one todo) — callers must not blindly retry an accepted add.
- RewordTodo(proof, todo, title) -> ChangeOutcome. Views: fix-a-todo-s-wording, work-the-todo-list. Usable -> RewordTodo(member, todo, trimmed); unusable (blank) -> StrikeTodo(member, todo) (retitle-to-blank removes). Then postlude. Idempotent. Todo absent -> ErrTodoNotFound (no tally, no publish).
- RemoveTodo(proof, todo) -> ChangeOutcome. Views: remove-a-todo, work-the-todo-list. StrikeTodo(member, todo), then postlude. Idempotent: an already-removed todo (e.g. removed by the other actor) succeeds.
- MarkTodo(proof, todo, completed) -> ChangeOutcome. Views: mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done, work-the-todo-list. MarkTodo(member, todo, completed), then postlude. Idempotent. Todo absent -> ErrTodoNotFound (no tally, no publish).
- MarkEveryTodo(proof) -> ChangeOutcome. Views: mark-everything-done-at-once-and-undo-it, work-the-todo-list. The caller does not choose the direction; the Manager decides against current state (natureOfTheBusiness rule): TallyItemsLeft(member); if itemsLeft == 0 (every todo already completed, including the empty list) -> MarkEveryTodo(member, completed=false), else -> MarkEveryTodo(member, completed=true). Then postlude (the second tally). The bulk write is atomic in TodoListAccess, so a single request never leaves a mixed state.
- ClearCompleted(proof) -> ChangeOutcome. Views: sweep-away-finished-todos, work-the-todo-list. PurgeCompleted(member), then postlude. Idempotent; active todos untouched.
- ReviewList(proof, view) -> ListReview. Views: review-the-todo-list, switch-between-all-active-and-done-todos, find-the-list-as-it-was-left-on-returning, use-the-todo-list-embedded-in-an-mcp-hosted-screen, see-how-many-todos-are-left. Read-only: changes nothing, publishes nothing. RecallList(member) (whole list in added order; completedCount = number completed in it); for view active/completed -> SelectInView(member, view) gives todos; for view all the recalled list IS the view (SelectInView may be skipped, as in see-how-many-todos-are-left); TallyItemsLeft(member) -> itemsLeft. The recall, select and tally may run concurrently (fork n5 / join n8). Empty or unset view is ErrInvalidRequest (clients default to all). Safe and idempotent.

ERROR MODEL (exported sentinels; the only errors that cross the contract — no storage, identity-scheme or bus types leak):
- ErrActorRefused (terminal): proof not recognized. Clients map to unauthenticated/forbidden.
- ErrIdentityUnavailable (transient): identity provider unreachable within the bounded wait; caller may retry.
- ErrTodoNotFound (terminal): the named todo is not in the recognized member's list (includes another member's todo; never revealed). Clients should re-read with ReviewList.
- ErrInvalidRequest (terminal): empty todo id, or view outside all/active/completed (maps TodoListAccess ErrInvalidArgument).
- ErrListUnavailable (transient): TodoListAccess ErrRecordUnavailable after the Manager's bounded wait; the request did not complete; retrying idempotent ops is safe.
Any other downstream fault is wrapped as ErrListUnavailable, never a hang or raw technical error. Every downstream call runs under a bounded wait (identity ~2s, record ~5s) derived from the caller's context.

IDEMPOTENCY: all ops except AddTodo are idempotent; ReviewList is side-effect free. CONCURRENCY: last-committed-write-wins (TodoListAccess exposes no version); accepted for this release — a person and an assistant acting at once each get a consistent whole-list result, and toggle-all always applies one uniform state. Live conflict signalling is deferred to the change-propagation volatility (future subscribers/live updates absorbed behind Publish, no op change).

FACTORING DECISIONS: one facet; the seven ops are exactly the seven behaviours the committed inbound edge and the 13 dynamic views name, each reached (TP-OP-REACHED). Collapsing them into a generic ApplyChange(kind, ...) was rejected — it would hide the business verbs, turn the contract into a dispatcher and push UI flow into a discriminator. Splitting reads (ReviewList) from writes was rejected — one cohesive facet over one list; a 1-op contract is a red flag. No GetX/SetX: MarkEveryTodo takes no direction (the toggle rule is the Manager's), ReviewList returns a business view, not raw state. Rejected/omitted: Subscribe/live push (no view calls it), undo, sharing, member id params.

REUSE: any channel (new protocol, new UI host) reuses this contract unchanged; a second team keeping a todo list behind recognized actors would implement the same seven verbs; swapping the store, identity scheme or bus transport changes none of them.

APP C SS6 CHECK: 1 reusable PASS. 2a PASS (7 ops). 2b WAIVED: 7 ops, above the 3-5 target — the committed System fixes these seven behaviours on every inbound edge and each is a distinct business verb called by its own dynamic view; the only collapses available (generic dispatcher, read/write split) worsen cohesion. 2c PASS (7 <= 12). 2d PASS. 3 PASS (no property-like ops, no CRUD shape). 4 PASS (1 contract). 5 PASS (designed by senior-developer; junior constructs only). 6 PASS (senior-developer designer, system-architect reviewer).

RESOLVED SRS QUESTIONS: Q1 sync, publish fire-and-forget; Q2 publish failure logged, request succeeds; Q3 last-write-wins, atomic bulk toggle; Q4 refused add is accepted=false (not an error) and, per the committed graph, still tallies + publishes; Q5 ListChanged = topic + member scope only; Q6 writes return itemsLeft (AddTodo also the new todo), channels re-read via ReviewList; Q7 ErrTodoNotFound for reword/mark, remove is idempotent success; Q8 trim, non-empty, no cap; Q9 opaque ActorProof passed through; Q10 7 ops, waived above.

Todo.description: One item in a member's list.

todoListAccess.notes:
STATUS: FROZEN, once architect review passes. DESIGNER: senior-developer. REVIEWER: system-architect.

FACET: one contract, TodoListAccess, covering the team-owned durable record of each member's todo list. It encapsulates record-storage volatility (which store) and hosting-environment volatility (where it runs and how it is configured). Sole caller: TodoKeepingManager, synchronously. Sole resource: TodoStore (Postgres), synchronously. It publishes and subscribes to nothing and imports no Temporal. Every operation is scoped to the supplied member, who has already been recognized by the Manager.

OPERATIONS:
- RecordTodo(member, title) -> Todo: appends a new active todo at the end of the member's list and returns it with a freshly minted opaque TodoID. The title is stored exactly as given. Title acceptance is the Manager's job. Not idempotent: each success appends one todo.
- RewordTodo(member, todo, title): overwrites the title without reordering. Idempotent. Returns ErrTodoNotFound if the todo is absent.
- StrikeTodo(member, todo): permanently removes one todo. Idempotent: an already-absent todo succeeds as a no-op, so a retry, or a person and an assistant removing the same todo at once, is safe. This also serves the Manager's reword-to-empty path.
- MarkTodo(member, todo, completed): sets one todo's completed state without reordering. Idempotent. Returns ErrTodoNotFound if the todo is absent.
- MarkEveryTodo(member, completed): sets every todo in the member's list to that state in one transaction (all or nothing). Idempotent. The toggle-all decision is the Manager's job.
- PurgeCompleted(member): removes every completed todo in one transaction and leaves active ones untouched. Idempotent.
- RecallList(member) -> TodoList: the member's whole list in added order, exactly as last committed, surviving restarts. An unknown member gets an empty list.
- SelectInView(member, view) -> TodoList: the member's todos that match the view (all, active or completed), in added order. Filtering may happen in the store or over the recalled list; only the result is contractual.
- TallyItemsLeft(member) -> ItemsLeft: the count of the member's active todos, consistent with every write already committed.

ERROR MODEL (every operation returns error; the package exports sentinel errors, checked with errors.Is):
- ErrTodoNotFound (terminal): the todo is not in the supplied member's list. This includes another member's todo, which is never revealed or acted on.
- ErrInvalidArgument (terminal): empty member, empty todo id, or a view outside all/active/completed.
- ErrRecordUnavailable (transient, safe to retry): the store cannot be reached, or the write could not be committed.
No SQL state, driver type or storage id crosses the contract.

IDEMPOTENCY AND CONSISTENCY: all writes except RecordTodo are idempotent, and reads have no side effects. Every write is committed before it returns. Bulk writes are atomic. Added order is stable. Concurrent writers get last-committed-write-wins, and no version is exposed: conflict handling belongs to change-propagation, which the Manager owns. Access is parameterised only.

ORCHESTRATION GUIDANCE (non-normative, for the Manager's Activity wrapper): StartToClose 5s. Retry only ErrRecordUnavailable. ErrTodoNotFound and ErrInvalidArgument are terminal.

HOSTING: the connection settings come from configuration (never hard-coded or exposed). The component creates or migrates its own schema idempotently at start-up, so the same code runs on a laptop trial and on house Postgres.

APP C SS6 CHECK: 1 reusable PASS (business verbs only, store-agnostic). 2a PASS. 2b WAIVED: 9 ops, above the 3-5 target. The committed system design fixes the nine atomic business verbs, each called by a dynamic view. They form one cohesive facet over one record, and splitting reads from writes would break cohesion. 2c PASS (9 <= 12). 2d PASS. 3 PASS: no Get/Set pairs and no CRUD shape. 4 PASS: 1 contract. 5 and 6 PASS: designed by senior-developer, reviewed by system-architect.

IDEMPOTENCY: all ops except AddTodo are idempotent; ReviewList is side-effect free. CONCURRENCY: last-committed-write-wins (TodoListAccess exposes no version); accepted for this release — a person and an assistant acting at once each get a consistent whole-list result, and toggle-all always applies one uniform state. Live conflict signalling is deferred to the change-propagation volatility (future subscribers/live updates absorbed behind Publish, no op change).

FACTORING DECISIONS: one facet; the seven ops are exactly the seven behaviours the committed inbound edge and the 13 dynamic views name, each reached (TP-OP-REACHED). Collapsing them into a generic ApplyChange(kind, ...) was rejected — it would hide the business verbs, turn the contract into a dispatcher and push UI flow into a discriminator. Splitting reads (ReviewList) from writes was rejected — one cohesive facet over one list; a 1-op contract is a red flag. No GetX/SetX: MarkEveryTodo takes no direction (the toggle rule is the Manager's), ReviewList returns a business view, not raw state. Rejected/omitted: Subscribe/live push (no view calls it), undo, sharing, member id params.

REUSE: any channel (new protocol, new UI host) reuses this contract unchanged; a second team keeping a todo list behind recognized actors would implement the same seven verbs; swapping the store, identity scheme or bus transport changes none of them.

APP C SS6 CHECK: 1 reusable PASS. 2a PASS (7 ops). 2b WAIVED: 7 ops, above the 3-5 target — the committed System fixes these seven behaviours on every inbound edge and each is a distinct business verb called by its own dynamic view; the only collapses available (generic dispatcher, read/write split) worsen cohesion. 2c PASS (7 <= 12). 2d PASS. 3 PASS (no property-like ops, no CRUD shape). 4 PASS (1 contract). 5 PASS (designed by senior-developer; junior constructs only). 6 PASS (senior-developer designer, system-architect reviewer).

RESOLVED SRS QUESTIONS: Q1 sync, publish fire-and-forget; Q2 publish failure logged, request succeeds; Q3 last-write-wins, atomic bulk toggle; Q4 refused add is accepted=false (not an error) and, per the committed graph, still tallies + publishes; Q5 ListChanged = topic + member scope only; Q6 writes return itemsLeft (AddTodo also the new todo), channels re-read via ReviewList; Q7 ErrTodoNotFound for reword/mark, remove is idempotent success; Q8 trim, non-empty, no cap; Q9 opaque ActorProof passed through; Q10 7 ops, waived above.

actor-identity-access.content:
# ActorIdentityAccess — Requirements (scope note)

Activity: C-actor-identity-access (coding, 10 effort-days, junior-developer, risk bucket 2). Contract key: actorIdentityAccess. Layer: ResourceAccess.

## Encapsulated volatility
Actor-identity volatility (axis: all customers at one time; traces B-01, B-09): how a team member is recognized, and how a team assistant (agent tooling) is authorized to act on that member's list on their behalf. Teams differ in identity scheme (company sign-in, simple accounts) and delegation scheme (tokens, delegated grants), and agent-delegation conventions are still settling. This component exists so that no other component knows which scheme is in use.

## Responsibilities (each traces to a committed System edge)
1. Recognize the actor behind a presented proof as a team member, or refuse it — the single atomic business verb RecognizeActor (System: atomicBusinessVerbs; edge todo-keeping-manager → actor-identity-access, sync, "RecognizeActor(proof) → member | refused").
2. Treat a team assistant acting under a delegation grant as the delegating member (assistants act with the same abilities as a person) — or refuse it when the grant does not verify (dynamic views: "verify the member proof or the assistant delegation grant").
3. Verify member proofs and assistant delegation grants against the team's identity provider (edge actor-identity-access → team-identity-provider, sync, "verify proof and delegation").
4. Keep the identity/delegation scheme, the provider's protocol and its vocabulary entirely behind this boundary: callers see only "member" or "refused".

Out of scope: anything about todos or lists (TodoListAccess), deciding what a recognized member may do with a list (the Manager's workflow), session/UI concerns (clients), notifications (bus). No other edges touch this component; it publishes and subscribes to nothing.

## Callers / consumers
- todo-keeping-manager — the only caller, synchronously, as the first step of every one of the 13 dynamic views (work/review the list, add, fix wording, remove, mark done/not done, mark all and undo, sweep finished, agent tooling drives the list, switch active/done, count remaining, find list on returning, embedded MCP-hosted screen). It is therefore on the hot path of every use case.

## Downstream dependency
- team-identity-provider (Resource, external): the authority that verifies proofs and delegation grants. Synchronous call.

## Non-functional constraints
- Security: fail closed — any proof or grant that cannot be positively verified (malformed, expired, revoked, provider unreachable) yields "refused", never a default member. Never log or echo raw proofs/grants/secrets. An assistant must never be recognized as a member other than the one who delegated to it. Treat the provider's responses as untrusted input.
- Maintainability: a junior-developer activity; keep the surface to the one business verb and the provider details private, so a scheme change is a change inside this component only.
- Extensibility: swapping or adding an identity scheme (company sign-in vs simple accounts) or delegation scheme (tokens vs delegated grants) must not change the caller-facing contract or the Manager.
- Performance/availability: called synchronously on every use case, so recognition latency adds to every request; provider unavailability must surface as a distinguishable refusal/failure rather than a hang (bounded wait).
- Statelessness per ResourceAccess rules: no business logic, no calls up or sideways; only reached from the Manager.
- Testability: must be exercisable with a fake/stub identity provider so the Manager and this component can be tested without the real provider.

## Open questions for Detailed Design
1. What does "member" carry back to the Manager — just an opaque member identity, or also whether the actor was an assistant acting on the member's behalf (e.g. for audit)? The committed edge says only "member | refused".
2. Should "refused" distinguish causes (bad proof vs provider unavailable) so the Manager/client can respond differently, without leaking the scheme?
3. Which concrete scheme(s) does the first release support? Operational Concepts (slot 6) and Required Behaviors (slot 2) are not committed, so provider choice and infra building block are unresolved.
4. Is any caching of verification results permitted (latency vs revocation freshness)?
5. What proof shape does the Manager pass through — a neutral opaque credential so clients' channel details don't leak into the contract?

message-bus.content:
# MessageBus — Requirements scope note (C-message-bus)

**Layer:** Utility (`kind: utility`, contract key `messageBus`). **Encapsulated business volatility:** none — the committed System gives `encapsulates: ""` and no `encapsulatesVolatilities`. This is expected for a Utility: it is cross-cutting plumbing, not a business seam. The business volatility it *serves* is **Change-propagation volatility** (how and when an actor on one channel learns of changes made through another), but the committed System assigns that volatility to **TodoKeepingManager**, not to the bus. The bus is the mechanism the Manager uses; the Manager owns the policy.

## 1. Responsibilities (each traced to a committed edge)

| # | Responsibility | Trace in committed System |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Accept a `ListChanged` publication from TodoKeepingManager after a member's list has been changed. | relationship `todo-keeping-manager → message-bus` (sync, `publish(ListChanged)`) |
| R2 | Be the final step of every **state-changing** use case, after the change is persisted and items-left is re-tallied. | dynamic views: `work-the-todo-list` n19, `add-a-todo` n9, `fix-a-todo-s-wording` n9, `remove-a-todo` n6, `mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done` n6, `mark-everything-done-at-once-and-undo-it` n9, `sweep-away-finished-todos` n9, `let-the-team-s-agent-tooling-drive-the-list` n6 |
| R3 | Play **no** part in read-only use cases. | not present in `review-the-todo-list`, `switch-between-all-active-and-done-todos`, `see-how-many-todos-are-left`, `find-the-list-as-it-was-left-on-returning`, `use-the-todo-list-embedded-in-an-mcp-hosted-screen` |
| R4 | Decouple the publisher from whoever later reacts to a list change, so that the Manager does not know or call the reactors directly. | follows from R1 + the Manager owning Change-propagation volatility (the publish edge is its only propagation edge) |

Nothing else is in scope. In particular, the bus does not persist todos, tally items left, recognise actors, or decide *what* counts as a change. Those belong to TodoListAccess, ActorIdentityAccess, and TodoKeepingManager.

## 2. Callers / consumers

- **Callers (publishers):** TodoKeepingManager only. It is the sole inbound edge in the committed relationships and in all 8 dynamic views that touch the bus.
- **Consumers (subscribers):** **none are modelled** in the committed System. There is no `message-bus → *` edge and no subscribe/deliver step in any dynamic view. See open question Q1.
- **Downstream calls:** none. The bus calls no other component and no Resource in the committed design.

## 3. Non-functional constraints

**Maintainability**
- Must stay message-agnostic plumbing. Todo semantics (what a list, todo, or view is) must not leak into it, or the bus ends up sharing the Manager's volatility.
- Must be small and independently testable by a test client that publishes without a real Manager.

**Extensibility**
- Adding a reactor to list changes (for example, a client that wants live updates as expectations move from "correct on return" to "live") must not require changing the publisher. This is the reason the edge exists, per the Change-propagation volatility rationale.
- The delivery mechanism must be replaceable without touching callers. The trial runs on a single box and later moves to the team's standard infrastructure (see Hosting-environment volatility).

**Security**
- Each member keeps their own list. Change notices about one member's list must never be observable by another member's actors or by an assistant without that member's delegation. The bus must not become a side channel around ActorIdentityAccess.
- Notices should carry no more of the list than consumers need. The less member data passes through the bus, the smaller the exposure.

**Operational / quality bars**
- Publishing is the Manager's last step on every state-changing call, so the bus is on the hot path of every write. Publishing must not noticeably delay the caller and must not block on any consumer.
- The change is already persisted when publish is called. A failure inside the bus must not corrupt or roll back the stored record.

## 4. Scope of the work (beyond coding)

Estimate: 10 days (junior developer, risk bucket 2). The work covers more than coding:
- Choosing or learning the transport, in-process or brokered (depends on Q4).
- A test client and harness that act as both publisher and probe subscriber.
- Integration with TodoKeepingManager (C-todo-keeping-manager) as the first and only caller.
- Short usage documentation for future subscribers.

## 5. Open questions for Detailed Design

- **Q1 — Who subscribes?** The committed System models only the publish side. Is the bus expected to serve subscribers in this release (for example, clients pushing live updates)? Or is it a forward seam with no consumer yet? If consumers exist, the System needs the missing edges via an architect amendment; this phase must not invent them.
- **Q2 — Operational concepts are not committed.** The `operationalConcepts` slot has no committed model, so the sync/queued and pub/sub treatment of this edge is unconfirmed. Does the `sync` mode on `publish(ListChanged)` mean the hand-off is synchronous with fan-out decoupled from the caller, or does the caller wait for delivery?
- **Q3 — Delivery guarantee and ordering.** Is at-most-once acceptable (consumers re-read on demand, matching "correct on return"), or is at-least-once with per-member ordering required?
- **Q4 — Transport and hosting.** Is in-process delivery acceptable for the single-box trial? Must it be swappable for a brokered transport on the team's infrastructure without contract change?
- **Q5 — Publish failure policy.** If publishing fails after the change is persisted, should the Manager's operation still succeed? This is the Manager's decision, but it constrains what the bus must report.
- **Q6 — Message ownership.** Who defines the `ListChanged` shape (member scope, which list, whether items-left travels with it)? Does the bus treat it as opaque?
- **Q7 — Subscriber authorization.** If consumers exist (Q1), where is member scoping enforced: at subscription, at delivery, or by the consumer after calling ActorIdentityAccess?

todo-keeping-manager.content:
# TodoKeepingManager — Requirements (scope note)

Activity: C-todo-keeping-manager (coding, 25 effort-days, junior-developer, risk bucket 5). Layer: Manager. Contract key: todoKeepingManager. Depends on C-actor-identity-access, C-message-bus and C-todo-list-access, whose contracts are already frozen. C-todo-api, C-todo-mcp-server, U-SPA-todo-web-app and U-SPA-embedded-todo-screen all wait on this activity. That puts it at the centre of the network, and its contract gates all four clients.

This note covers scope only: what the component must do, who calls it, and the quality bars it must meet. It proposes no operations, signatures or data shapes. Those belong to Detailed Design.

## 1. What it encapsulates

**Change-propagation volatility.** This is the order in which each list change happens: recognize the actor, apply the change, re-tally items left, then make the change known to the other channels. It also covers how and when an actor on one channel learns about a change made on another. Today that means correct on return. Later it may mean live, as assistant use grows. Concurrent-edit conflict (a person and an assistant at once) was folded into this volatility, so it is the Manager's concern.

It is the only Manager in the system. Every use case runs through it. It owns the workflow. The business verbs belong to the ResourceAccess components it calls.

## 2. Callers and consumers

There are four callers. All are Clients, all call synchronously, and all have the same committed inbound edge: `AddTodo | RewordTodo | RemoveTodo | MarkTodo | MarkEveryTodo | ClearCompleted | ReviewList — works or reviews the todo list`.
- **todo-web-app**: the browser app team members use.
- **embedded-todo-screen**: the same screen embedded in an MCP-hosted UI host.
- **todo-api**: the ordinary web API that assistants and agent tooling call.
- **todo-mcp-server**: the MCP tools that assistants call.

The four channels must get identical behaviour. This is the reason the Manager exists: neither the assistant-protocol volatility nor the human-presentation volatility may fork the todo rules.

It calls three components downstream, all synchronously:
- **actor-identity-access**: `RecognizeActor(proof) → member | refused`.
- **todo-list-access**: `RecordTodo | RewordTodo | StrikeTodo | MarkTodo | MarkEveryTodo | PurgeCompleted | RecallList | SelectInView | TallyItemsLeft`.
- **message-bus**: `publish(ListChanged)`.

No Engine exists or is called. Nothing calls the Manager except the four Clients. It subscribes to nothing.

## 3. Responsibilities (each traced to a committed edge or dynamic-view step)

| # | Obligation | Trace |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Recognize the actor first, on every request: a team member, or an assistant acting for that member. If recognition is refused, do not touch the list. | n3 → actor-identity-access in all 13 dynamic views |
| R2 | Route a working request to the one change it asks for: add, retitle, remove, complete or reopen, toggle all, or clear completed. | work-the-todo-list n4 (decision "Which change was asked for?") |
| R3 | Add: accept the wording only if it is a usable title, then have the new active todo recorded at the end of the list. Otherwise refuse, and add nothing. | work-the-todo-list n6/n7/n8; add-a-todo n5 → RecordTodo |
| R4 | Retitle: if the new wording is usable, have the title reworded. If it is blank, have the todo struck from the list. | work-the-todo-list n10/n11/n12; fix-a-todo-s-wording n5 RewordTodo, n6 StrikeTodo |
| R5 | Remove one todo. | work-the-todo-list n14; remove-a-todo n4 → StrikeTodo |
| R6 | Mark one todo completed or active. | work-the-todo-list n15; mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done n4 → MarkTodo |
| R7 | Toggle all: decide whether to complete every todo, or reopen every todo when all are already completed, then apply that one state to the whole list. | work-the-todo-list n16; mark-everything-done-at-once-and-undo-it n5/n6 → MarkEveryTodo(completed=true / false) |
| R8 | Clear completed: purge every completed todo and leave active ones untouched. | work-the-todo-list n17; sweep-away-finished-todos n5 → PurgeCompleted |
| R9 | After every change, re-tally items left across the whole list, so the acting channel shows the current count. | work-the-todo-list n18 and the tally step of every change view → TallyItemsLeft |
| R10 | After every state-changing request, make the change known to the member's other open channels. | work-the-todo-list n19 and the last step of add / fix-wording / remove / mark / mark-everything / sweep / agent-tooling → message-bus publish(ListChanged) |
| R11 | Review: recall the member's list in added order, select the todos that belong in the chosen view (All / Active / Completed), and tally items left. Change nothing and publish nothing. | review-the-todo-list n4 RecallList, n6 SelectInView, n7 TallyItemsLeft (n5 fork / n8 join); the same in switch-between-views, find-the-list-as-it-was-left, embedded-mcp-screen. see-how-many-todos-are-left uses RecallList + TallyItemsLeft |
| R12 | Give assistants the same abilities and the same rules as a person, through the agent-tooling channels. | let-the-team-s-agent-tooling-drive-the-list (same downstream chain via todo-api / todo-mcp-server) |

The Manager keeps two rejected volatilities as plain logic, because the volatility analysis found them to be variables, not seams. One is the usable-title predicate (title-acceptance, `variableNotVolatile`). The other is the toggle-all decision rule (`natureOfTheBusiness`). Neither justifies an Engine. The Manager makes both decisions. TodoListAccess only carries them out.

**Out of scope:** storage, durability and ordering of the record (TodoListAccess); the identity and delegation scheme (ActorIdentityAccess); delivery mechanics and subscribers (MessageBus); presentation, gestures (Enter / Escape), showing the current view, and protocol encoding (Clients). Undo/redo, sharing, offline sync, reminders, audit, reporting and extra todo attributes are all explicitly rejected.

## 4. Non-functional constraints

**Security**
- Fail closed. A refused or unverifiable actor gets no read and no write. Nothing about the list leaks in a refusal.
- Per-member scope. The member that ActorIdentityAccess returns is the only member whose list is touched. A caller must never be able to name a different member. An assistant acts only for the member who delegated to it.
- Treat all caller input (titles, todo references, view choice) as untrusted. Never log raw proofs or credentials.

**Correctness and ordering**
- Write path: recognize → change → tally → publish, in that order. Publish only after the change is persisted, so subscribers that re-read see the new state.
- The tally returned to the acting channel must reflect the change made by the same request.
- The toggle-all decision must be made against current list state. Concurrent person and assistant requests must not leave the list in a mixed state that no single request asked for (see Q3).
- A refused add (an unusable title) changes nothing. Whether it still re-tallies or publishes is open (see Q4).

**Maintainability**
- This is a junior-developer activity with the highest risk bucket (5). Keep the workflow readable as the orchestration of the use-case activity diagrams. No storage, identity-scheme, protocol or transport details may enter the Manager.
- Must be testable in isolation with fake ResourceAccess and bus implementations, and must also be exercised end to end through each dynamic view.

**Extensibility**
- A new client channel or protocol (assistant-protocol or human-presentation volatility) must reuse the Manager unchanged.
- A move from correct-on-return to live updates should be absorbed by what the Manager publishes and how, plus new subscribers. It should not require rewriting each behaviour.
- Swapping the store or the identity scheme must not change the Manager.

**Operational**
- Synchronous request/response on every inbound and outbound edge, with nothing queued. Every request is on the hot path of four calls (identity, change, tally, publish), so each dependency needs a bounded wait. A dependency failure must surface as a business-meaningful outcome, never as a hang or a leaked technical error.
- Load is trivial (load/scale volatility was rejected), so no caching or scaling machinery is needed.
- Stateless between calls. The record lives only in TodoListAccess.

## 5. Scope of the work (beyond coding)

The 25 days cover more than writing the workflow:
- learning the three frozen dependency contracts;
- integration with all three dependencies;
- a test client per use case that drives all 13 dynamic views, including refusal, blank-retitle, toggle-all both ways and the read-only paths;
- fakes for the dependencies;
- documentation the four client activities can build against.

Because four activities depend on it, the contract should freeze early and stay stable.

## 6. Open questions for Detailed Design

1. **Operational concepts are not committed.** The sync/queued and pub/sub treatment of the publish edge is unconfirmed. Is publishing fire-and-forget from the Manager's point of view?
2. **Publish failure policy.** If the change is persisted but publishing fails, does the request still succeed for the caller? (The MessageBus scope note left this to the Manager.)
3. **Concurrency.** Is last-write-wins acceptable when a person and an assistant act at once, especially for toggle-all, which reads state and then writes? Or does the Manager need a conflict signal from TodoListAccess?
4. **Refused add.** On an unusable title, does the caller get an explicit refusal outcome, and is the re-tally / publish skipped? The diagram merges the refused path back into the tally and publish steps.
5. **What travels in ListChanged.** Member scope only, or also items left or the kind of change? It must carry no more member data than subscribers need.
6. **What a write returns to the acting channel.** The diagram's last note says "the acting channel shows the updated list and items left". Is that the updated list, the tally, the changed todo, or a combination?
7. **Not-found and stale todos.** What is the outcome when a retitle, remove or mark targets a todo that is already gone, for example one removed by the other actor?
8. **Usable-title rule.** It is "not empty or whitespace-only" today. Should titles be trimmed before storing? Is there a length cap?
9. **Identity proof.** How does the proof pass from each Client through the Manager in a channel-neutral form, so that no Client's protocol details reach the contract?
10. **Cardinality of the inbound surface.** The committed edge lists seven behaviours. Detailed Design must check that against the 3–5 (max 12) operations guidance, without changing the behaviours.

todo-list-access.content:
# TodoListAccess — Requirements (scope note)

Activity: C-todo-list-access · Layer: ResourceAccess · Contract key: todoListAccess

This is a scope note. It covers what the component must do, who calls it, and the quality bars it must meet. It does not propose operations, signatures or data shapes. That is Detailed Design's job.

## 1. What it encapsulates

- **Record-storage volatility.** Where, and in what kind of store, the team-owned durable record of each member's list lives. Today that is a single-file store for a trial. Later it may be a managed database or a self-hosted store.
- **Hosting-environment volatility**, as it affects the record. Process lifetime, configuration and the location of the store change when hosting moves from a laptop to house infrastructure. None of this may reach the Manager.

The atomic business verbs are fixed by the committed system design: RecordTodo, RewordTodo, StrikeTodo, MarkTodo, MarkEveryTodo, PurgeCompleted, RecallList, SelectInView, TallyItemsLeft. They are business verbs over a member's list, not CRUD or storage verbs. Storage specifics stay behind them.

## 2. Callers and consumers

- **Sole caller: TodoKeepingManager** (`todo-keeping-manager -> todo-list-access`, sync). Every use case reaches the record only through the Manager. No Client, Engine or other ResourceAccess calls this component.
- **Sole downstream: TodoStore** (`todo-list-access -> todo-store`, sync, "read and write the member list").
- It does not publish to or subscribe on MessageBus. The ListChanged publication is the Manager's edge (`todo-keeping-manager -> message-bus`). It does not call ActorIdentityAccess. The member arrives already recognized, from the Manager.
- Both edges are synchronous request/response. Nothing is queued.

## 3. Responsibilities (each traced to a committed edge)

All responsibilities are scoped to one member's own list. The member is always supplied by the Manager.

| # | Obligation | Traces to (dynamic-view step / store edge) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Durably keep a new todo as active, at the end of the member's list, and return it | RecordTodo: work-the-todo-list n7, add-a-todo n5, agent-tooling n4. Store: "append the new active todo at the end of the list" |
| R2 | Replace one todo's title | RewordTodo: work-the-todo-list n11, fix-a-todo-s-wording n5. Store: "overwrite the todo title" |
| R3 | Remove one todo permanently. This also covers the Manager's reword-to-empty path | StrikeTodo: work-the-todo-list n12/n14, fix-a-todo-s-wording n6, remove-a-todo n4. Store: "delete the one todo" |
| R4 | Set one todo's completed state | MarkTodo: work-the-todo-list n15, mark-a-todo-done-or-not-done n4. Store: "set the todo completed flag" |
| R5 | Set every todo in the member's list to one completed state. The Manager makes the toggle-all decision, using the tally | MarkEveryTodo: work-the-todo-list n16, mark-everything-done n5/n6. Store: "set every todo completed flag" |
| R6 | Remove every completed todo and leave active ones untouched | PurgeCompleted: work-the-todo-list n17, sweep-away-finished-todos n5. Store: "delete every completed todo" |
| R7 | Return the member's whole list in the order the todos were added, exactly as last left, across visits, closed windows and restarts | RecallList: review-the-todo-list n4, switch-between-views n4, see-how-many-left n4, find-the-list-as-it-was-left n4, embedded-mcp-screen n4. Store: "read the member's todos in added order" |
| R8 | Return the member's todos that match a view (All / Active / Completed) | SelectInView: review-the-todo-list n6, switch-between-views n5, find-the-list-as-it-was-left n5, embedded-mcp-screen n5. Store: "read the member's todos matching the view" |
| R9 | Return the count of the member's active todos, current after every change | TallyItemsLeft: on every use case's tally step (e.g. work-the-todo-list n18, review-the-todo-list n7). Store: "count the member's active todos" |

Out of scope here: title acceptance (empty or whitespace), the toggle-all decision, identity and delegation checks, change notification, and presentation. These belong to the Manager, ActorIdentityAccess, MessageBus and Clients respectively, per the committed relationships.

## 4. Non-functional constraints

**Durability and correctness**
- Every completed state change must be durable before the call returns. A later RecallList, even after a service restart, must reflect it. This is the return-visit guarantee (B-09).
- Bulk changes (R5, R6) must apply to the whole list or not at all. A partially toggled or partially purged list is never visible.
- Added order is preserved and stable. Reword and mark never reorder.
- The tally and view selections must be consistent with the list state that the same request just wrote.

**Security and isolation**
- Strict per-member isolation. No responsibility may read, change or count another member's todos. An item that does not belong to the supplied member is treated as not found and is never acted on.
- Store credentials and location come from configuration. They are never hard-coded and never exposed to the caller.
- Titles are stored as given. Parameterised access only, so there is no injection path into the store.

**Maintainability and extensibility**
- Swapping the store (single file, managed SQL, self-hosted) must be a change confined to this component. The Manager and its contract stay untouched.
- No storage types, errors, IDs or query concepts leak through the contract. Failures surface as business-meaningful outcomes, for example "no such todo" or "record unavailable".
- Stateless between calls apart from the store connection. It must be safe under concurrent calls from the same member, for example a person and an assistant at once. The last committed write wins, with no corruption.
- Load is trivial (small team). No caching or scaling machinery (load/scale volatility was rejected as speculative).

**Testability**
- Each responsibility must be testable against a real store instance and against a disposable or empty store. Restart-survival (R7) and per-member isolation must be directly testable.

## 5. Open questions for Detailed Design

1. **Operational concepts are not committed yet.** The concrete trial store and the house-infrastructure store (the go.mod already carries pgx/Postgres) must be confirmed before choosing the first adapter.
2. **Todo identity.** Who mints a todo's identity, and how stable and opaque it is across a store migration.
3. **Not-found and stale-item outcomes.** What a reword, strike or mark on an already-removed todo returns. This matters when a person and an assistant act at once.
4. **Concurrency stance.** Is last-write-wins enough, or should the record expose a version so the Manager can detect conflicting edits? Concurrent-edit conflict was folded into change-propagation volatility, which the Manager and MessageBus own.
5. **Tally after a write.** Should state-changing verbs also return the new tally, or does the Manager always call TallyItemsLeft separately? The dynamic views currently show it as separate calls.
6. **View selection in the store vs. over RecallList.** Whether SelectInView is a store-side selection or a filter over the recalled list is a Detailed Design choice. The obligation is only the result.
